<!-- https://fuzzloom.pages.dev/docs/cli.html -->

# CLI reference

```text
fuzzloom <command> [path] [options]
```

`path` is the Fe ingot to work on, a directory with `fe.toml` and `src/`. It defaults to the current directory.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `fuzzloom doctor [path]` | Checks Node, fe and its version, that the bundled Fe library compiles with your fe, the native backend, and the project's targets. Exits 2 if a required piece is missing |
| `fuzzloom list [path]` | Lists every target with its signature, effects, fixtures and declared ranges, and every skipped function with the reason |
| `fuzzloom fuzz [path]` | Runs every property campaign, plus one mutation campaign per saved failure, then recovers and shrinks any abort |
| `fuzzloom diff [path]` | Compares keyed checkpoints on sonatina and native and verifies the located mismatch |
| `fuzzloom reproduce <id> [path]` | Replays one saved failure from its stored input, with no random generation |
| `fuzzloom replay [path]` | Replays every saved failure: `FIXED` when it now passes, `FAILS` when it still fails, `REGRESSED` when a fixed one is back |

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--seed <n>` | Base seed. The CLI prints the seed so the input stream can be repeated |
| `--digest-key <n>` | Reuse the recorded checkpoint key for `diff`. The default is sampled independently of the campaign seed |
| `--runs <n>` | Positive input count per property (default 10,000) or differential target (default 100,000) |
| `--backend <b>` | `sonatina` (EVM, the default) or `native` |
| `--only <text>` | Select targets or saved failures whose name contains the text. The source CLI exits 2 if none match |
| `--no-corpus` | `fuzz` without the mutation campaigns around saved failures |
| `--uniform` | In 0.1.2, sample within the declared bounds with edge bias, argument correlation and corpus mutation disabled |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--junit <file>` | Also write a JUnit XML report: findings are `<failure>`, infrastructure problems are `<error>` |
| `-h`, `--help` | The usage text |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Everything passed |
| `1` | A property failed or aborted, or the backends diverged |
| `2` | An infrastructure error: a compile error, out of gas, a timeout, a missing backend or unreadable output. Never a finding |

## Result lines

| Line | Command | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `PASS` | `fuzz` | No input failed; the next line says what the campaign exercised |
| `FAIL` | `fuzz` | The property returned `false`; the shrunk and original inputs follow |
| `ABORT` | `fuzz` | The property panicked or reverted; the recovered and shrunk input follows |
| `AGREE` | `diff` | Identical digests on both backends |
| `DIVERGE` | `diff` | The first differing input, with both outputs |
| `INFRA` | any | Something outside your code went wrong; see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.html) |

## Files

| Path | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `.fuzzloom/failures/<target>-<hash>.json` | One saved failure: the shrunk and original inputs, seed, iteration, backend and fe version. Commit these |
| `.fuzzloom/tmp/` | Generated test harnesses. Removed when a command ends, kept only after an infrastructure error |

## Environment

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `FE_BIN` | `~/.fe/bin/fe`, else `fe` on `PATH` | The fe binary |
| `FE_WSL_DISTRO` | the default distro | Windows: the WSL distro that runs native tests |
| `FE_WSL_BIN` | `~/.fe/bin/fe` | Windows: fe inside WSL |
| `FUZZLOOM_TIMEOUT_MS` | `600000` | Per `fe` invocation |
| `FUZZLOOM_INGOT` | the bundled copy | Use a different checkout of the Fe library |
| `NO_COLOR` | unset | Plain output |


---

<!-- https://fuzzloom.pages.dev/docs/architecture.html -->

# Architecture

Fuzzloom has two halves with a strict split.

- **The Fe library** ([`ingots/fuzzloom`](../ingots/fuzzloom/src)) holds every testing algorithm: random generation, shrinking, mutation and differential digests. It runs inside `fe test`, on whichever backend executes it.
- **The TypeScript CLI** ([`packages/cli`](../packages/cli/src)) orchestrates. It discovers targets, generates test harnesses, runs `fe`, classifies the output, searches when the library cannot report an input, and stores failures.

The CLI never generates inputs or shrinks anything that Fe can shrink. The only algorithms in TypeScript are the ones that need information Fe cannot hand back: recovering the input of an abort, shrinking by replay, and comparing two backends. Exact guarantees for each algorithm are in [algorithms.md](algorithms.md).

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph CLI["packages/cli"]
    direction LR
    DISC["discover.ts<br/>targets, effects,<br/>fixtures, ranges"] --> ENG["engine.ts<br/>rounds and searches"]
    ENG --> HAR["harness.ts<br/>generated ingots"]
    ENG --> FE["fe.ts<br/>run and classify"]
    FE --> ABI["abi.ts<br/>decode payloads"]
    ENG --> STORE["store.ts<br/>failure records"]
    ENG --> REP["report.ts, junit.ts<br/>terminal, JSON, JUnit"]
  end
  subgraph LIB["ingots/fuzzloom"]
    direction LR
    RNG["rng"] --> GEN["gen, bias, draw"]
    GEN --> CHK["check, property, shrink"]
    GEN --> MUT["mutate"]
    GEN --> DIF["diff"]
    CHK & MUT & DIF --> PAY["payload"]
  end
  HAR -. "imports" .-> LIB
  FE -- "fe test (sonatina)" --> X1["generated ingot"]
  FE -- "fe test --backend native" --> X2["generated ingot"]
```

## The Fe library

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `rng.fe` | xorshift64\* generator, splitmix64 seed derivation, unbiased bounded sampling |
| `word.fe` | The `Word` trait: every argument type to and from a `u256` word (zigzag for signed) |
| `input.fe` | `Input` (up to three words) and `Bounds` (an inclusive word range per argument) |
| `gen.fe`, `bias.fe` | Uniform ranges and boundary-biased edges |
| `draw.fe` | The campaign input stream: biased per-argument draws plus correlated draws; `generated_at` |
| `property.fe` | `prop1/2/3` wrappers: any callable returning `bool`, its effect row forwarded |
| `shrink.fe` | Sweep, greedy descent and joint moves |
| `check.fe` | Campaigns (`find`, `check`, `check_bounded`), `replay`, `input_at` |
| `mutate.fe` | Mutation campaigns around a saved input: `check_mutating`, `mutant_at`, `mutated_at` |
| `diff.fe` | `Target` and `target1/2/3`; digests, checkpoints, `evaluate`, `target_input_at` |
| `payload.fe` | The `#[error]` structs that carry every result out of Fe |

**Generic over effects.** A property is any `Fn` returning `bool`. The wrappers declare `uses E = F::E`, so a property's effects flow through `check(...)` to the caller, who provides them with `with`. The library therefore never needs to know which effects a user's code has. A generic callable needs `uses F::E` at every level, and the library is written that way throughout.

**Results leave as reverts.** A test function cannot return data to `fe test`, but a revert payload is printed. Every harness entry point (`check`, `replay`, `input_at`, `digest_checkpoints`, `evaluate`, and so on) ends with exactly one `revert_error(...)` of a payload struct. `std::evm::revert_error` works on both backends, and the payload bytes are identical on each; the known-answer digest test checks this.

**Bounded variants.** Each entry point has a `_within` form, or takes `bounds` directly, so a declared input range applies to the campaign, recovery, mutation and digests alike. `target_bounds_of(t)` exists because an associated-function call on a generic type cannot appear in a harness expression in fe 26.6.

## The CLI

### Discovery (`discover.ts`)

Discovery reads every `.fe` file under `src/`, with comments blanked so commented-out code is ignored and line numbers stay right. It matches `pub fn prop_*` and `pub fn diff_*` signatures, including ones that `fe fmt` wrapped across lines. For each match it:

1. parses the parameters and keeps each argument's label: positional (`_ x`), the name, or an explicit label;
2. parses a `uses (...)` clause into effect types;
3. reads `/// fuzzloom: <arg> in <lo>..=<hi>` lines directly above the function into word ranges ([`bounds.ts`](../packages/cli/src/bounds.ts));
4. resolves each effect to exactly one fixture, by return type or else by snake-case name;
5. computes the Fe import paths for the target, its effect types and its fixtures from the file layout (`src/a/b.fe` is `<ingot>::a::b`).

Anything that cannot be tested is returned as skipped, with the reason.

### Harness generation (`harness.ts`)

A harness is a throwaway ingot under `<your ingot>/.fuzzloom/tmp/<label>-<backend>/`. Its dependencies use relative paths, so the same file works for Windows `fe.exe` and for fe inside WSL. Every case becomes one `#[test]`. For the bounded, effectful vesting property in `examples/token-ledger`:

```fe
// Generated by the Fuzzloom CLI. Do not edit.
use fuzzloom::*
use token_ledger::policy::Clock
use token_ledger::policy::fixture_clock
use token_ledger::prop_vested_never_exceeds_total

#[test]
fn case_0() {
    check_bounded(prop2(|a0: u128, a1: u64| {
        var e0 = fixture_clock()
        with (Clock = e0) { prop_vested_never_exceeds_total(a0, start: a1) }
    }), bounds: bounds_of(prop2(|a0: u128, a1: u64| {
        var e0 = fixture_clock()
        with (Clock = e0) { prop_vested_never_exceeds_total(a0, start: a1) }
    })).restrict(1, lo: 0x6372bd80, hi: 0x6553f100), seed: derive_seed(7, 0x5f4a556c0d9d1a2c), runs: 10000)
}
```

The closure is repeated rather than bound to a variable because Fe closures are not `Copy`. A target without effects is passed directly as a function item (`prop2(prop_withdraw_never_overdraws)`).

Harness modes:

| Mode | Fe entry point | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | `check`, `check_bounded`, `check_mutating(_within)` | A campaign, fresh or around a saved input |
| `replay` | `replay` | One saved or candidate input |
| `input_at` | `input_at`, `mutant_at(_within)` | The input at an iteration, without evaluating it |
| `replay_at` | `replay` of `generated_at` / `mutated_at` | Evaluating that input in the same test |
| `checkpoints` | `keyed_checkpoints_within` | Up to 256 keyed prefix digests in one pass |
| `target_input_at` | `target_input_at(_within)` | The input a digest drew at an iteration |
| `evaluate`, `evaluate_at` | `evaluate` | One differential output |

### Running fe and classifying (`fe.ts`, `abi.ts`)

`runBatch` runs `fe test --color never [--backend native] <dir>`. On Windows the native backend goes through `wsl -- bash -lc`, with the path translated by `wslpath`. Both backends of a differential round run concurrently. The output is split into one block per `PASS|FAIL [time] name` line, and each block is classified on its own (see [algorithms.md, section 10](algorithms.md#10-classifying-outcomes)). A missing result line is `unparsed`, never a pass. A compile error, which produces no result lines at all, applies to every test in the batch.

Selectors in `abi.ts` are computed with keccak-256 from the signatures, which mirror `payload.fe` field for field. They are never hardcoded, and a test checks them against selectors the Fe compiler actually emitted.

### The engine (`engine.ts`)

The engine thinks in **rounds**. Each `fe test` invocation compiles once, so every evaluation that does not depend on another goes into the same generated ingot.

| Command | Rounds |
|---|---|
| `fuzz` | 1 round: every property's campaign, plus one mutation campaign per saved failure. For each abort: k-ary search rounds on the run count, 1 recovery round (`input_at` + `replay_at`), then shrink-by-replay rounds |
| `diff` | 1 round on each backend at once: 256 checkpoints per target. For each divergence: search rounds of one checkpoint test per backend, then 1 recovery round |
| `replay`, `reproduce` | 1 round per backend that has records, both at once |

Results are combined per target in a fixed order of precedence:
1. the fresh campaign's failure, abort or infrastructure outcome;
2. otherwise, the first mutation campaign that failed, aborted or hit infrastructure;
3. otherwise, a pass.

### Failure records (`store.ts`)

`.fuzzloom/failures/<target>-<fnv8>.json`, version 1. The id is a hash of the target name and the shrunk input, so finding the same minimal failure again updates the record instead of duplicating it.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "id": "prop_withdraw_never_overdraws-2c81bbb3",
  "kind": "property",
  "target": "prop_withdraw_never_overdraws",
  "args": [{ "name": "balance", "type": "u128" }, { "name": "amount", "type": "u128" }],
  "input": ["0x0", "0x1"],
  "values": ["0", "1"],
  "original": ["0xa2a5905cfacdaa5f06766da86b098bbb", "0xa2a5905cfacdaa5f06766da86b098bbc"],
  "iteration": "18",
  "base_seed": "7",
  "runs": "10000",
  "backend": "sonatina",
  "fe_version": "fe 26.6.0 (5b3f96a)",
  "status": "open"
}
```

`kind` is `property`, `abort` (with `detail`, the panic reason) or `differential` (backend `both`, with both outputs in `detail`). A record found by a mutation campaign carries `seeded_by`. Records are only ever replayed with their stored input, so they stay valid when the generator changes. `replay` refuses a record whose target changed signature, and says so.

### Reports (`report.ts`, `junit.ts`)

There are three outputs. The terminal output uses colour unless `NO_COLOR` is set or output is not a TTY. `--json` output preserves every field, with bigints as strings. `--junit` writes one test case per property, differential target or saved failure: findings are `<failure>`, infrastructure is `<error>`, and text is escaped, stripped of colour and of characters XML cannot carry.

## Packaging

The npm package `fuzzloom` contains compiled JavaScript (`dist/`), because Node does not strip TypeScript types under `node_modules`. It also contains a copy of the Fe library (`ingot/`), made by the `prepack` script. `libraryIngot()` prefers a repository checkout when running from source, so a stale bundled copy never shadows the live library, and falls back to the bundled copy in an installed package. CI packs the package, installs it into an empty prefix and runs it on a project outside the repo, checking that the bundled library is the one used.

## Constraints that shaped the design

| Constraint (fe 26.6) | Design response |
|---|---|
| A test can only report through a revert payload | Every entry point ends with one ABI-encoded `#[error]`; the CLI decodes by selector |
| Fe cannot catch a panic, so an abort carries no input | A deterministic, prefix-consistent stream, k-ary search on the run count, and shrinking by replay |
| `fe test` compiles once per invocation | Rounds: every independent case in one generated ingot |
| Each EVM test is capped at 10^9 gas | Campaign sizes chosen to fit; out-of-gas is classified as infrastructure, never as a finding |
| The native backend runs on Linux and macOS only | Native runs through WSL on Windows; `doctor` reports its availability |
| `Evm` effects are a type error on native | Differential testing compares shared logic; effects come from user fixtures |
| Fixed-size arrays are not allowed in custom errors | Checkpoints use `DynArray<u256>` built from a `MemVec` |
| Closures are not `Copy` | The harness repeats the closure expression |
| An `Fn` impl with a forwarded effect row, called through a generic bound, crashes the compiler | The library avoids that shape; reproduction in [`spike/compiler-bugs`](../spike/compiler-bugs/fn-impl-forwarded-effect) |


---

<!-- https://fuzzloom.pages.dev/docs/algorithms.html -->

# Algorithms and their guarantees

Every non-trivial algorithm in Fuzzloom states what it guarantees and where it stops, and has a test that fails if the guarantee breaks. This page collects them. Each section names its source and the tests that enforce it. Fe tests run on both the sonatina (EVM) and native backends; CLI tests run under Node.

1. [Random numbers](#1-random-numbers)
2. [Input encoding](#2-input-encoding)
3. [Input generation](#3-input-generation)
4. [Shrinking inside Fe](#4-shrinking-inside-fe)
5. [Recovering the input of an abort](#5-recovering-the-input-of-an-abort)
6. [Shrinking by replay](#6-shrinking-by-replay)
7. [Differential digests and checkpoints](#7-differential-digests-and-checkpoints)
8. [Mutation around saved failures](#8-mutation-around-saved-failures)
9. [Choosing the search width](#9-choosing-the-search-width)
10. [Classifying outcomes](#10-classifying-outcomes)

## 1. Random numbers

**Source:** [`ingots/fuzzloom/src/rng.fe`](../ingots/fuzzloom/src/rng.fe)

**Generator.** xorshift64\* (Vigna, 2014): one 64-bit state word, shifts and one multiplication. It is small and fast on both backends, and fully specified in the source, so a seed replays the same stream everywhere. A zero seed is remapped so the state is never stuck at zero.

**Per-property seeds.** `derive_seed(base, id) = splitmix64(base ^ splitmix64(id))`, where the CLI passes the 64-bit FNV-1a hash of the property name as `id`. Without this, every property in a run would draw the same stream and share its blind spots. A mutation campaign derives its seed from the property name together with the saved input.

**Uniform ranges.** `below_or_eq(max)` uses masked rejection sampling. It accepts a `bit_len(max)`-bit candidate when it is at most `max`. With independent, uniform bits this avoids modulo bias and needs fewer than two draws in expectation. Fuzzloom uses a deterministic 64-bit-state PRNG. At a given iteration it can produce at most `2^64` different 256-bit outputs across all seeds. The CLI's uniform mode disables edge substitutions, argument correlation and corpus mutation while keeping that PRNG. Maxima below 2^64 use one 64-bit word per attempt. A full-width maximum such as `2^256 - 1` accepts the assembled word in one attempt.

| Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|
| Same seed, same stream; different seeds diverge; a zero seed is not stuck | `same_seed_same_stream`, `different_seeds_diverge`, `zero_seed_is_not_stuck` |
| The stream matches a recorded reference | `known_answer_vector`, `splitmix64_matches_reference_vectors` |
| In the measured seed, the test detects the skew that reduction modulo `max + 1` would introduce on a range covering about 2/3 of the 256-bit domain | `below_or_eq_is_unbiased_for_non_power_of_two_ranges` |
| Results never exceed `max`, including full-width maxima | `below_or_eq_respects_bound`, `below_or_eq_handles_full_width_maxima`, `full_width_maxima_use_the_exact_mask_path` |
| Derived seeds differ per property and per base seed | `derived_seeds_differ_per_property_and_base` |

**Limit:** not cryptographic. That is fine for test generation and wrong for anything else.

## 2. Input encoding

**Source:** [`word.fe`](../ingots/fuzzloom/src/word.fe), [`input.fe`](../ingots/fuzzloom/src/input.fe)

Generation, shrinking, payloads and records all work on `u256` words, so one generic runner serves every type. Unsigned integers map to themselves and `bool` maps to 0 and 1. Signed integers use **zigzag** encoding: 0, -1, 1, -2, 2 map to words 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. Word order then follows magnitude, so shrinking toward word 0 shrinks toward zero from both sides. The generic range edges also land on the signed edges: the top word is `MIN`, and the word below it is `MAX`.

An input is up to three words. Words past the property's arity are always zero. `Bounds` gives every argument an inclusive word range, and its lower end is also the shrink floor.

| Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|
| Every type round-trips at its maximum; every `i8` round-trips | `round_trips_at_the_type_maximum`, `signed_round_trip_every_i8`, `signed_round_trip_wide_values` |
| Zigzag order is magnitude order; extremes sit at the top words | `zigzag_orders_by_magnitude`, `zigzag_extremes_sit_at_the_top_words` |

**Consequence:** a contiguous signed range is only expressible as a contiguous word range when it is centred on zero. That is why `/// fuzzloom:` annotations on signed arguments must be `-k..=k` or `-(k+1)..=k`.

## 3. Input generation

**Source:** [`gen.fe`](../ingots/fuzzloom/src/gen.fe), [`bias.fe`](../ingots/fuzzloom/src/bias.fe), [`draw.fe`](../ingots/fuzzloom/src/draw.fe)

**Boundary bias.** Defects cluster at edges, so one argument draw in four (`Biased::of`, `every: 4`) comes from the edge table instead of the uniform range: `lo`, `hi`, `lo + 1`, `hi - 1`, the midpoint, and `lo + 2^k - 1`, `lo + 2^k`, `lo + 2^k + 1` for a random `k` that keeps the value in range.

**Correlation.** For two or more arguments, one draw in eight (`CORRELATE_EVERY`) sets argument 1 to argument 0, one above it, or one below it. If that value does not fit argument 1's bounds, the inverse relation is applied to argument 0 instead, so arguments of very different widths still correlate. Whole bug classes live on that diagonal: transfer to self, `amount == balance`, off-by-one between two inputs. Two independent 128-bit draws essentially never land on it.

**Determinism.** The input at iteration `i` is a pure function of (bounds, arity, seed, i). Every campaign, every recovery and every digest draws through the same `draw` function.

**Statistics.** A passing campaign reports how many argument draws were edge values, how many inputs were correlated, and a bitmask of which argument bounds were reached. A pass is therefore a measured claim, not just a run count.

| Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|
| Every draw respects every argument's bounds; unused words stay zero | `draws_respect_bounds_per_argument`, `unused_arguments_stay_zero`, `edges_stay_in_range` |
| Edges reach full-width extremes, and bias finds the top of `u64` far more often than uniform draws | `edges_hit_full_width_extremes`, `biased_finds_top_of_u64_far_more_than_uniform` |
| Correlation hits the diagonal, including across widths, and finds off-by-one bugs | `correlation_hits_the_diagonal_of_wide_arguments`, `correlation_works_across_argument_widths`, `correlated_generation_finds_off_by_one_between_arguments` |
| `generated_at(i)` reproduces the stream; tracking statistics does not change it | `generated_at_replays_the_stream`, `tracking_does_not_change_the_stream` |
| The statistics measure what was exercised | `stats_measure_what_the_campaign_exercised`, `passing_campaign_reports_what_it_exercised` |

**Limit:** the edge table is a fixed set of patterns, not learned from the code under test. Only the first two arguments are correlated.

## 4. Shrinking inside Fe

**Source:** [`shrink.fe`](../ingots/fuzzloom/src/shrink.fe)

When a property returns `false`, the campaign shrinks the failing input in the same test, within a budget of 5,000 evaluations (`SHRINK_BUDGET`).

**One argument**, in two phases, neither needing the failure to be monotone:

1. **Sweep:** try `lo, lo + 1, ..., lo + 255` (`SWEEP = 256`) and take the first that fails. Small counterexamples are the most readable, and this finds them exactly.
2. **Greedy descent:** from the best failing word, try the floor, then `best - 2^k` for `k` from the top bit of the distance down to 0. The first candidate that still fails becomes the new best, and the scan restarts. Exact powers of two matter. Steps of `best / 2^j` can all share a parity, which under zigzag means they all share a sign, and the descent would stall on the first input.

**Several arguments**, in rounds until a round changes nothing. Each round shrinks one coordinate at a time with the others fixed. It then tries three **joint moves**:
- all arguments to the floor;
- all distances divided by their gcd, or halved;
- all lowered by the same `2^k`.

Joint moves escape relations such as `a == b`, `b == a + 1` and `b == 2a`, where every single-coordinate move passes.

**Guarantee, when `complete` is true:** the result fails, and none of these passes, so the result is a local minimum under those moves:
- replacing one argument's word `w_i` by `w_i - 2^k >= lo_i`, with the others fixed;
- lowering every argument by the same `2^k`;
- dividing every distance by the gcd or by 2.

When the budget runs out, `complete` is false and the result is the best failing input found, which still fails.

| Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|
| A threshold failure shrinks to the exact threshold; everything-fails shrinks to the floor | `shrinks_threshold_failure_to_the_threshold`, `shrinks_to_floor_when_everything_fails` |
| Non-monotone failures are handled; a passing value is never returned | `handles_non_monotone_failures`, `never_returns_a_passing_value` |
| A complete result is a verified local minimum, checked by trying every move | `complete_result_is_a_verified_local_minimum`, `three_argument_result_is_a_coordinate_wise_local_minimum`, `complete_result_is_minimal_under_scaling_moves` |
| Joint moves escape diagonals and proportional relations | `joint_move_escapes_a_diagonal`, `proportional_relations_shrink_to_smallest_ratio` |
| The budget is respected; power-of-two steps cross parity (sign) | `respects_budget`, `power_of_two_steps_cross_parity` |

**Limit:** a local minimum, not necessarily the global one.

## 5. Recovering the input of an abort

**Source:** [`check.fe`](../ingots/fuzzloom/src/check.fe), [`packages/cli/src/engine.ts`](../packages/cli/src/engine.ts) (`recoverAbort`, `searchFirst`)

Fe cannot catch a panic or a revert. A property that overflows or divides by zero ends the test with a raw `Panic` payload and no input. Fuzzloom recovers the input anyway.

**Prefix consistency.** The campaign stream is deterministic and the campaign stops at its first failure. So a campaign of `k` runs aborts exactly when `k` is past the first aborting iteration. It cannot instead return a counterexample: the first failing input and its shrink are the same for every such `k`, so that shrink would abort too. "Aborts at `k` runs" is therefore false, then true, as `k` grows.

**k-ary search.** `searchFirst(lo, hi, width, probe)` finds the smallest `k` with a monotone predicate known true at `hi`. Each round probes up to `width` run counts in one batched `fe` run. The probes form the arithmetic progression `hi - s, hi - 2s, ...` with `s = floor((hi - lo) / (width + 1)) + 1`. Every gap between probes, and the gap below the lowest, then holds at most `floor((hi - lo) / (width + 1))` undecided values.

**Guarantee:** the exact smallest aborting run count, in at most `ceil(log_(width+1)(runs))` rounds. One more round asks for `input_at(iteration)`, which evaluates nothing and cannot abort, and `replay_at(iteration)` together. An abort from the replay means the property itself aborts on that input. A plain `false` means the property fails normally and the in-Fe shrinker hit an aborting candidate. Both cases are reported as such.

| Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|
| Failures are prefix-consistent in the campaign (and in mutation campaigns) | `prefix_consistent_failures`, `mutation_campaign_failures_are_prefix_consistent` |
| `generated_at` recovers the failing input | `generated_at_recovers_the_failing_input` |
| `searchFirst` returns the exact minimum within the round bound, swept over widths 1, 2, 7, 21 and 64, sizes up to 10,000 and dense answer positions | CLI: `searchFirst finds the exact minimum within the stated round bound` |
| The probes are evenly spaced and every gap meets the bound | CLI: `probePoints is an evenly spaced progression whose gaps meet the roundsFor bound` |

**Limit:** the property must be deterministic. Fixtures make effectful properties deterministic by building fresh state for every evaluation.

## 6. Shrinking by replay

**Source:** `shrinkByReplay`, `shrinkCandidates`, `jointCandidates` in [`engine.ts`](../packages/cli/src/engine.ts)

An aborting input cannot be shrunk inside Fe, because the abort ends the test. The CLI shrinks it by replaying candidates, all of one round in a single `fe` run. Candidates act on each argument's distance from its floor: the lower end of a declared range, else 0.

- **Single moves:** set one argument's distance to 0, or shift it right by 1, 2, 4, 8, and so on.
- **Joint moves**, offered when at least two distances are nonzero:
  - set every distance to 0;
  - divide every distance by their gcd `g`, and by each of 2, 3, 5 and 7 that divides `g`, or halve them all when `g` is 1;
  - subtract the same `d` from every distance, for `d` in `m`, 1, `m >> s` and `m - (m >> s)`, where `m` is the smallest distance.

Each round accepts the reproducing candidate with the fewest total bits, then the smallest sum. "Reproducing" demands the same failure: the same panic code or revert message for an abort. Shrinking therefore cannot slide onto a different bug.

**Guarantee, when complete:** no candidate move from the result reproduces, which makes it a local minimum under those moves. No candidate ever leaves the declared range. At most 8 rounds by default.

| Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|
| The result is a local minimum, checked by enumerating every move | CLI: `reaches the stated local minimum and never accepts a non-reproducing candidate` |
| Diagonal (`b == a + 1`) and proportional (`b == 2a`) failures that stall single moves are walked down | CLI: `joint moves walk a diagonal failure ...`, `joint moves follow a proportional failure ...` |
| The documented limit: `(96, 192)` for `b == 2a, a >= 3` ends at `(4, 8)`, a local minimum, not the global `(3, 6)` | CLI: same test |
| No candidate goes below a declared floor | CLI: `replay shrinking never leaves the declared range` |

## 7. Differential digests and checkpoints

**Source:** [`diff.fe`](../ingots/fuzzloom/src/diff.fe), `runDiffs` and `localiseDivergence` in [`engine.ts`](../packages/cli/src/engine.ts)

**Digest.** The CLI splits each 256-bit output into three base-`2^126` digits and feeds them most significant first into `acc = (acc * key + digit) mod p`, starting at zero, with `p = 2^127 - 1`. Every digit is strictly less than `p`, so distinct output sequences of equal length give distinct coefficient sequences. The Fe reducer adds the low 127 bits to the high bits, using `2^127 ≡ 1 (mod p)`. A single conditional subtraction suffices because the unreduced sum is below `2p`. The unkeyed Fe API still produces its original FNV-style checksum.

**Checkpoints.** `keyed_checkpoints_within` folds once and returns the digest after `first + j * step` inputs for every `j < count` (at most 256) in a `DynArray<u256>` payload. Each prefix depends only on its inputs and key, so overlapping prefixes agree across rounds on the same backend.

**Collision bound.** With deterministic streams fixed independently of an initially uniform nonzero key, two different length-`k` prefixes collide with probability at most `(3k - 1)/(p - 1)` over the sampled key. Before the first differing output, prefix digests always agree. For one target, sum the bound over the probes on the collision-free search path. The path is fixed independently of the key, and the actual adaptive search can first depart from it only at one of those probes. Sum across targets for a campaign-wide bound. The probability applies to a fresh draw and gives no unconditional guarantee for a fixed key.

**Search.** The first round probes evenly spaced checkpoints through the full run count. Subsequent rounds narrow the interval using the arithmetic progressions in section 5. A final round reports a finding only when both backends evaluated the same input and returned different outputs. If the candidate fails validation, the CLI reports `unlocated` as an infrastructure result. A collision can hide a mismatch or lead the search to a later real mismatch. The CLI records the independent key in text, JSON and JUnit. `--digest-key` reuses it for an exact rerun of the comparisons.

| Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|
| Each checkpoint equals the digest at its run count exactly | `every_checkpoint_equals_the_digest_at_its_run_count` |
| The old checksum can reconverge after two differing output words | `legacy_checksum_reconverges_on_two_words` |
| Field arithmetic matches an integer-modulo reference at limb boundaries | `keyed_fold_matches_integer_modulo_reference` |
| A fixed key can collide at the first output | `keyed_fold_can_collide_even_on_the_first_word` |
| The digest is the fold of exactly the generated inputs | `digest_is_the_fold_of_the_generated_inputs` |
| A single differing output changes the digest; seed and run count matter | `digest_detects_a_single_differing_output`, `digest_depends_on_seed_and_runs` |
| Both backends compute the same fold, generator and PRNG: one recorded constant checked on each | `known_answer_digest_matches_on_every_backend` |
| The real `Checkpoints` payload decodes and matches separate digest tests on both backends | CLI: `integration: real checkpoints equal separate digests, on both backends` |
| Generated keyed checkpoints match an independent BigInt reference on both backends | CLI: `integration: keyed checkpoints match a BigInt reference on both backends` |

## 8. Mutation around saved failures

**Source:** [`mutate.fe`](../ingots/fuzzloom/src/mutate.fe)

A mutation campaign explores the neighbourhood of one saved input instead of the whole input space. Each mutant starts from the saved input, clamped into bounds, and stacks 1 to 4 operators (`MAX_STACK`):
- a small step up or down;
- a single bit flip;
- an edge value;
- halving or doubling the distance from the floor;
- a copy of another argument, plus or minus one;
- a fresh uniform draw.

Mutants never accumulate, so every one stays near the saved input. `fuzz` adds one mutation campaign per saved failure, up to 8 per property, to its first round.

**Why:** after a fix, the exact saved input passes. A fix that special-cases only that input leaves its neighbours failing. A fresh campaign almost never lands there again; a mutation campaign does.

| Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|
| Every mutant is within bounds, even from a corpus outside them; words past the arity stay zero | `mutants_stay_within_bounds`, `arguments_past_arity_stay_zero` |
| `mutated_at(i)` reproduces the stream, and failures are prefix-consistent | `mutated_at_reproduces_the_stream`, `mutation_campaign_failures_are_prefix_consistent` |
| It finds a 7-value incomplete-fix window around a `u256` corpus that a fresh 2,000-run campaign misses | `mutation_finds_an_incomplete_fix_that_fresh_campaigns_miss` |
| The copy operator reaches correlated neighbours | `copy_operator_reaches_correlated_neighbours` |

**Limit:** value-level operators only, with no dictionary of constants taken from the code under test. A seed uses the shrunk input, not the original.

## 9. Choosing the search width

**Source:** `chooseWidth`, `roundsFor` in [`engine.ts`](../packages/cli/src/engine.ts)

Every `fe test` invocation compiles its ingot once, about 2.4 s idle (`COMPILE_MS`), and each additional test costs about 85 ms (`CASE_MS`). `roundsFor(u, k)` is the worst-case number of rounds for `u` undecided values at width `k`. `chooseWidth` picks the `k` that minimises `roundsFor(u, k) * (COMPILE_MS + CASE_MS * k)`, up to 64. For 10,000 runs that is width 21 and 3 rounds, where plain bisection takes 14 steps. Differential search does not need this trade-off: one checkpoint test answers a whole round at width 256.

| Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|
| Bisection is the width-1 case (14 rounds for 10,000); width 21 needs 3 | CLI: `roundsFor and chooseWidth ...` |
| The first differential round fits one checkpoint test and leaves at most 39 of 10,000 run counts | CLI: `the first diff round fits one checkpoint case ...` |

**Limit:** the constants were measured on one machine. Under load the compile cost grows faster than the per-test cost, which shifts the best width by about 10%.

## 10. Classifying outcomes

**Source:** [`packages/cli/src/fe.ts`](../packages/cli/src/fe.ts), [`abi.ts`](../packages/cli/src/abi.ts)

`fe test` prints `PASS|FAIL [time] name` per test, in completion order, followed by that test's revert payload or halt reason. The CLI splits the output per test name and decodes each payload by its selector. Selectors are computed with keccak-256 from the signatures, never hardcoded.

| Outcome | Classified as |
|---|---|
| A Fuzzloom payload | a result |
| `Panic(uint256)` or `Error(string)` | an abort from the user's code |
| An `OutOfGas` halt | infrastructure: `out-of-gas` |
| A compile error | infrastructure: `compile`, applied to every test in that ingot |
| No result line for a test, `PASS` without a payload, an unknown selector, or a truncated payload | infrastructure: `unparsed` |
| A timeout or a missing native backend | infrastructure: `timeout`, `backend-unavailable` |

**Guarantee:** an infrastructure outcome is never reported as a failing property or a backend mismatch, and it stays attached to its own test.

| Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|
| Per-name parsing in completion order; out-of-gas stays on its own test; a missing name or a payload-less `PASS` is `unparsed` | CLI: `batch` tests in `fe.test.ts` |
| A compile error applies to every test | CLI: `batch output with a compile error applies it to every case` |
| A known selector with a truncated body is infrastructure, not a crash | CLI: `a known selector with a truncated body is infra, not a crash` |


---

<!-- https://fuzzloom.pages.dev/docs/experiments.html -->

# Backend parity and sampling experiments

## Fe integer semantics on Fe 26.6.0

`node scripts/check-integer-semantics.mjs` generates and compares Fe functions that call the compiler's actual integer operators. Seed 7 exercised 100,000 boundary-biased inputs per operation and type. All **116 keyed checkpoint campaigns** agreed across Sonatina and native, for **11.6 million input pairs**, and all **762 explicit edge evaluations** agreed. Backend agreement covers the sampled inputs and the reported outcomes.

| Operation | Signed widths | Unsigned widths | Inputs per operation and type | Campaigns agreeing |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Wrapping addition | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 | Same | 100,000 | 12/12 |
| Wrapping subtraction | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 | Same | 100,000 | 12/12 |
| Wrapping multiplication | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 | Same | 100,000 | 12/12 |
| Left shift | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 | Same | 100,000 | 12/12 |
| Arithmetic or logical right shift | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 | Same | 100,000 | 12/12 |
| Division | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 | Same | 100,000 | 12/12 |
| Remainder | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 | Same | 100,000 | 12/12 |
| Exponentiation | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 | Same | 100,000 | 12/12 |
| Widen to 256 bits | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 | Same | 100,000 | 10/10 |
| Truncate from 256 bits | 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 | Same | 100,000 | 10/10 |

For signed shifts the generator masks off the sign bit of the count. Explicit probes include width minus one, width, and width plus one where representable. Exponentiation limits the base and exponent to 0–3 to fit every type. Those campaigns repeatedly exercise a small domain. The division and remainder digests guard zero divisors and signed minimum divided by minus one so a trap cannot discard the checkpoint stream. The explicit evaluations exercise the original operations at those inputs. Both backends returned panic `0x11` for signed minimum divided by minus one at all six widths, and panic `0x12` on 84 division or remainder evaluations with zero divisors. Both returned zero for signed minimum modulo minus one.

The JSON report records the fixed comparison key, every operation and result, and each explicit edge outcome. Matching fingerprints can collide. The operator matrix also does not establish whether two agreeing backends implement the language specification correctly.

## Paired uniform sampling baseline

`node scripts/measure-sampling.mjs sonatina` and `node scripts/measure-sampling.mjs native` ran seeds 1–20 on the six planted failures in vault-math and token-ledger. Each seed and sampler had a budget of 10,000 inputs and used the property's declared bounds. The measurement disables mutation and shrinking. For aborts, it recovers the first failing prefix in batched Fe runs and counts those invocations. The two backends produced identical rows, including the first failure positions and run counts. Each backend used 28 actual Fe invocations across 240 trials. A trial's Fe run count measures participation in shared invocations.

| Target | Biased hits | Biased median first input | Biased Fe runs per trial | Uniform hits | Uniform median first input | Uniform Fe runs per trial |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `prop_fee_matches_exact_math` | 20/20 | 1 | 1 | 20/20 | 1 | 1 |
| `prop_withdraw_never_overdraws` | 20/20 | 20.5 | 1 | 0/20 | — | 1 |
| `prop_redeem_rounds_toward_vault` | 20/20 | 1 | 1 | 20/20 | 1 | 1 |
| `prop_share_price_defined` | 20/20 | 18.5 | 2–17 | 0/20 | — | 1 |
| `prop_transfer_conserves_supply` | 20/20 | 4 | 2–11 | 0/20 | — | 1 |
| `prop_vested_never_exceeds_total` | 20/20 | 1 | 2–7 | 20/20 | 1 | 2 |

The [paired results CSV](sampling-results.csv) records each seed, whether it found a failure, the first input when found, and the Fe run count for each sampler. The clearest wins came from inputs requiring a particular edge or a relation across arguments. The vesting defect already had a narrow declared range, and uniform sampling found it at the first input for all 20 seeds.
